discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated many-body physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices, from the superfluid-Mott insulator transition to the Fermi-Hubbard model

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and LMU Munich, Germany

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum many-body physics
motivation: Bloch, Greiner and Esslinger turned ultracold atoms in optical lattices into clean, fully controllable realizations of the Hubbard model, a central model of condensed-matter physics. Their 2002 observation of the quantum phase transition from a superfluid to a Mott insulator showed that a textbook many-body transition could be engineered and measured directly. They then extended this to fermions. Esslinger's group observed Fermi surfaces and the fermionic Mott insulator. Bloch's and Greiner's quantum-gas microscopes imaged single atoms and resolved antiferromagnetic correlations, magnetic polarons and entanglement at the single-site level. These techniques are now standard across the field. They created analogue quantum simulation as an experimental discipline, answering questions about correlated electrons that classical computation cannot settle, and they laid the foundations for today's neutral-atom quantum processors.
